source: Morgan (1894; 1903) Introduction to Comparative Psychology, via Wikipedia and Heyes 2012
finding: The canon says an animal act must not be read as a higher psychical faculty if a lower one can explain it. Morgan wrote it against Romanes' anecdotal, anthropomorphic method.
numbers: 1894 wording as quoted by Heyes, Bruni and Mikhalevich (p. 53). 1903 edition (p. 59): no animal activity is to be interpreted by higher psychological processes if it can be fairly interpreted by processes lower in the scale.
quote: In no case may we interpret an action as the outcome of the exercise of a higher psychical faculty
limits: Secondary quotation, not the 1894 book itself. Wording differs slightly across sources (faculty vs mental vs psychical).
agent_relevance: G3: a rule for what counts as an adequate explanation of a pass. Needs the 1903 rider to avoid denial of real ability.

source: Morgan 1903 rider (de Waal 2002 quoting Morgan), via Wikipedia
finding: Morgan later added that a higher explanation is fine if the species has shown independent signs of high intelligence.
numbers: No numbers.
quote: there is nothing really wrong with complex interpretations
limits: Paraphrase by Wikipedia of de Waal (2002); original 1903 text not opened.
agent_relevance: Prior evidence of capability can license the richer reading: treat a model's proven capability on a clean control as that independent sign.

source: C. Lloyd Morgan (Wikipedia biography): chicks and terrier Tony
finding: Morgan hatched chicks, ducklings and moorhens away from adults and logged behaviour to separate inherited from learned acts. His terrier Tony learned to open a garden gate by gradual steps, which Morgan used to argue insight was not needed.
numbers: Born 1852, died 1936. No trial counts given on the page.
limits: Single-animal observation; the Tony case is an anecdote he himself recorded.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as our agent: a pass that looks like insight may be slow trial-and-error accumulation; log the steps.

source: Pfungst (1911) Clever Hans, via Wikipedia
finding: Hans the horse answered by reading involuntary cues from the questioner. Pfungst isolated the horse, used other questioners, used blinders, and varied whether the questioner knew the answer.
numbers: Hans could see questioner: 50 of 56 correct (89%). Could not see questioner: 2 of 35 correct (6%). Stumpf commission of 13 members found no trick in Sept 1904.
limits: Wikipedia summary; separate accuracy for the questioner-ignorant condition not given there.
agent_relevance: Template for contamination and leak tests: remove the channel that carries the answer (blinders, ignorant questioner) and see whether the pass survives.

source: Heyes (2012) Simple minds: a qualified defence of associative learning
finding: Heyes names two errors: association-blindness and simple-mindedness. Associative learning is a contender, not a default winner. Morgan never justified the canon, and later evolutionary and simplicity defences fail. She asks for rival accounts specified well enough to give different predictions.
numbers: No sample sizes of her own. Horner et al. 2011: six female chimpanzees in a prosocial choice test, bias for dual-reward token only when a partner was present.
quote: a contender—a candidate explanation for intelligent behaviour in all animals—but not as a default winner
limits: Opinion/review. She does not discuss mindreading or scrub jays in this paper.
agent_relevance: Core design rule: write both the low-level and the high-level account as models that predict different outcomes, then run the discriminating test (G3), with no default for either.

source: Heyes (2012), ghost control proposal
finding: Concrete differential test: replay the unwrapping sound with the partner absent. If the prosocial bias stays, associative learning explains it. If it vanishes, the cognitive account gains.
numbers: No numbers reported for the proposed test.
quote: We need experiments—and then yet more experiments
limits: Proposed, not run in this paper.
agent_relevance: The best-practice shape for an LLM contamination or shortcut test: a control that keeps the cue but removes the task-relevant structure.

source: Heyes (2012), breadth of associative learning
finding: Conditioning appears in every major taxon studied, and in humans it predicts IQ beyond working memory and speed. Mirror-system responses can be reversed by counter-training.
numbers: MacPhail 1982 survey (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds): no counts given. Kaufman et al. 2009 on IQ: no coefficients given in the text.
quote: Evidence of associative learning has been found in every major taxon where it has been sought
limits: Counts and effect sizes are cited, not given.
agent_relevance: Low-level mechanisms are common, so they are a live baseline for any pass. Pattern matching in a model should be assumed possible, not excluded by default.

source: Penn and Povinelli (2007) On the lack of evidence that non-human animals possess anything remotely resembling a theory of mind
finding: Behaviour cues can predict an agent's acts with no mental-state variable. A mental-state account must do unique causal work beyond cues. They also say a folk-psychology account is simpler for us, not for the animal to implement.
numbers: Hare et al. 2001 chimp competitive food paradigm: only one critical metric significant (experiment 1, uninformed condition); misinformed condition not significant. No percentages in the text.
quote: any cognitive system, whether theory-like or not, that predicts or explains the behaviour of another agent
limits: Authors are sceptics; the paper is a review, not new data. Read first 100k of 124k characters.
agent_relevance: Test with variants where a cue-based rule and the intended reasoning give different answers. Same logic as Ullman's perturbations.

source: Penn and Povinelli (2007), proposed discriminating protocols
finding: They propose a five-bucket competitive design with nine conditions (removed uninformed, replaced, misinformed, swapped) and an opaque-visor begging test, because cue-based rules fail on these.
numbers: Visor: enculturated chimps failed (Vonk et al. 2005, unpublished); 18-month-old infants passed a blindfold version (Meltzoff 2007). Corvids: Emery and Clayton 2001 re-caching, Dally 2006, Bugnyar and Heinrich 2006 all explained by simple rules.
limits: Proposals; visor result is unpublished in the cited source.
agent_relevance: A model of a good battery: conditions where the shortcut and the true rule diverge. Use as the shape of a G3 held-out check.

source: Mikhalevich, Powell and Logan (2017) Is behavioural flexibility evidence of cognitive complexity?
finding: The canon is wrongly read as Occam's razor. A simple explanation does not mean a simple mechanism. Flexibility can be evidence of complex cognition once combined with ecology and neuroanatomy (the Adaptive Triadic Model). Their only real tie-breaker is more evidence.
numbers: Few numbers: cleaner wrasse has one of the largest diencephalons among 25 perciform species compared; other brain-size comparisons without figures.
quote: frequently, though incorrectly, interpreted as a version of Occam's Razor
limits: Read first 100k of 165k characters. Arguments are comparative, not experimental.
agent_relevance: Flexibility under changed conditions is the best behavioural sign of a rule rather than a habit: supports using mutated inputs as the test (G3).

source: Bruni, Perconti and Plebe (2018) Anti-anthropomorphism and its limits
finding: Seven criticisms of the canon: conflated with Occam, parsimony not clear-cut, Morgan was more liberal than followers, strict avoidance failed in practice, it guards only one error (anthropomorphism, not anthropodenial), burden-of-proof bias, reductio by analogy.
numbers: Hebb 1946 at Yerkes: strict avoidance of anthropomorphic description produced 'an almost endless series of specific acts' with no order. Cartmill 2000 anthroporenalism analogy.
quote: Neither can be omitted without renouncing the scientific method
limits: Quote is Morgan 1903 pp. 48-49 as cited. Review, no new data.
agent_relevance: Warns of a symmetric error for our agent: under-crediting a real capability costs as much as over-crediting. G3 tests should be able to confirm as well as deny.

source: Bruni et al. (2018), alternatives to the canon
finding: Alternatives: critical anthropomorphism (Burghardt), evidentialism (Fitzpatrick 2008), constructive anthropomorphism (Arbilly and Lotem 2017), animal-centred variants. Also cases where the richer reading later won: honey bee dance (von Frisch 1927), rat 50 kHz play chirps (Panksepp 1998).
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Selected examples; counterexamples chosen by the authors.
agent_relevance: Evidentialism is the usable rule: prefer the account the evidence favours, whichever level it sits on.

source: Mercado (2016) commentary on Starzak (2016) Interpretations without justification
finding: Starzak argues nothing justifies preferring explanations lower on the scale. Mercado adds that evidence rarely separates the explanations, so empiricism leaves deadlock, and strict canon use may bias researchers toward under-attributing.
numbers: No numbers.
quote: Morgan's Canon leads to unjustified verdicts about animals' minds, but empiricism gives rise to deadlocked juries
limits: Commentary on a paper not itself opened.
agent_relevance: Expect many tests to be undecided. The agent should report 'underdetermined' instead of forcing the simple reading.

source: Farrar, Ostojic and Clayton (2021) The hidden side of animal cognition research (survey)
finding: Researchers largely endorse the canon but many want caveats and many prefer plain parsimony. They admit hope for results and think replication is rare.
numbers: 210 completed of 1,001 invited (21.6%). 70.5% agree canon is important (31.9% strongly). 16 free-text comments caveat it; 30 stress parsimony. Hoping for a result: sometimes 39.7%, often 38.8%. Replication important: 89.6%. Not enough replications in own area: 70.8% disagree there are enough. Median predicted replication success 65% (IQR 50-75%).
quote: Morgan's canon often leads to more bias rather than less
limits: Self-selected 21.6% response; read first 100k of 202k characters.
agent_relevance: Even experts report hoping for outcomes. Our tests should be fixed in advance (pre-registered scoring) to avoid the same bias.

source: Voudouris, Farrar, Cheke and Halina (2025) Morgan's canon and the associative-cognitive distinction today
finding: Survey of over 200 comparative psychologists: they treat the canon as a parsimony principle, but do not see the associative-cognitive distinction as a version of the canon.
numbers: Over 200 respondents; no further numbers read.
limits: Only the abstract was seen via the Europe PMC API; full text not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports keeping two separate questions: which level of mechanism, and which account is simpler.

source: Auersperg (2025) Morgan's ghosts: On canon, cognition, and what we still do not know
finding: Commentary: the canon began as a call for rigour but became a rigid slogan, yet still limits over-interpretation, shapes designs and pushes researchers to specify mechanisms.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Abstract summary only.
agent_relevance: Useful framing: the canon as a discipline to specify mechanisms, not a verdict.

source: Sober / Fitzpatrick / Starzak line, via Heyes 2012, Wikipedia and Bruni 2018
finding: Sober showed Morgan's own Method of Variation is too permissive to justify the canon; Fitzpatrick (2008) proposes evidentialism; Starzak (2017) says the canon lacks operational hierarchies.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Secondhand. The primary Sober and Fitzpatrick texts were not opened (direct fetches failed).
agent_relevance: Do not hard-code a level hierarchy in the schema; the hierarchy is the weak part.

source: Kosinski (2023) Theory of mind may have spontaneously emerged in large language models
finding: 11 LLMs on 40 false-belief tasks. Newer models solved more. Author frames emergence as a possibility.
numbers: 640 prompts, 40 tasks, pass needs 16 prompts correct across 8 scenarios. Small and old models: 0%. davinci-003 and GPT-3.5-turbo: 20%. GPT-4: 75% (matches six-year-olds).
limits: Abstract page only. Ullman and Shapira later found the pass is fragile.
agent_relevance: A high-level reading of a pass (theory of mind) that the lower-level reading (surface cue) then contested. Exactly the canon pattern.

source: Ullman (2023) Large language models fail on trivial alterations to theory-of-mind tasks
finding: Small changes that keep theory of mind principles (transparent bag, reader cannot read, trusted friend, you wrote the label) make GPT-3.5 give the wrong belief. He argues failures outweigh averages, using a multiplication analogy.
numbers: Original unexpected-contents: popcorn 100%; belief prompt chocolate 99%. Variants: transparent 95% chocolate; cannot read 98%; trusted friend 97%; wrote the label 87%. Unexpected transfer variants: transparent 94%/90% wrong; in to on 97%/74%; trusted call 97%/94%. Second belief prompt in transparent case corrected from the first version (double space artifact).
quote: If one end of the scales has 20 successes and the other end a single failure, shouldn't the scales tip
limits: One model (GPT-3.5) and handpicked variants; no human control; token probabilities, not free text. A first version contained a prompt-spacing error, since corrected.
agent_relevance: The G3 mutated-input test in miniature: success on the given items is not proof; one structured failure is informative.

source: Ullman (2023), his Morgan-style conclusion
finding: Ullman states the simpler explanation: LLM belief reasoning is sensitive to small irrelevant perturbations, rather than the model changing its mind or forgetting.
numbers: Base popcorn bag: 14% popcorn and 82% chocolate on the second belief prompt; unexpected transfer base P(basket)=98%.
quote: a simpler explanation is that LLM reasoning about ToM is sensitive to small irrelevant perturbations
limits: Same GPT-3.5 only.
agent_relevance: Direct use of the canon in LLM evaluation: prefer the lower-level account until a perturbation test says otherwise.

source: Shapira et al. (2023) Clever Hans or Neural Theory-of-Mind?
finding: 15 LLMs on 6 ToM benchmarks plus the Adv-CSFB adversarial set. Some benchmarks solved, others at or below the most-frequent-class baseline. Performance drops with category and perturbation.
numbers: TriangleCOPA 96% (flan-t5-xxl). FauxPas-EAI 27% for GPT-4, below baseline. ToMi: GPT-3.5 70% total, 81% on one subset but 46% on false-belief questions. Siqa GPT-4 79% total, 61% on 'others' questions. GPT-4 97% on original false-belief but 0% on transparent access and 'in to on' (davinci-002 66.7% and 71.4%). 'Other person' fell 93.8% to 68.8%. Kosinski used 40 examples, Bubeck 10.
quote: models do not have robust N-ToM abilities
limits: Small Adv-CSFB sets written by the authors; MC-probing vs LM-probing differ (7% on Siqa for GPT-4).
agent_relevance: Report accuracy per category, not a single average; a category at 0% is the finding.

source: Shapira et al. (2023), explanation of the shortcut
finding: Authors suggest reporting bias (people state surprising rather than obvious facts) and instruction tuning (model assumes every detail matters) as sources of the shortcut.
numbers: Models regenerated answers repeatedly with similar results, so wrong answers were confident. True-belief examples may be helped by recency bias.
limits: Hypotheses, not tested by ablation.
agent_relevance: Prompt details that look relevant will be used. Strip or mark irrelevant detail before the answer step.

source: Strachan et al. (2024) Testing theory of mind in large language models and humans
finding: GPT-4, GPT-3.5, LLaMA2-70B versus 1,907 humans on false belief, irony, faux pas, hinting, strange stories. GPT-4 matched or exceeded humans on most; weak on faux pas due to hyperconservatism, while LLaMA2's faux pas strength was a bias.
numbers: Per-test N about 48-51 humans. Irony GPT-4 above humans (P=0.040). Faux pas GPT-4 below (P=5.42e-5); LLaMA2-70B above (P=0.002). Belief-likelihood test N=900 humans: GPT-4 'uncertain' in 42/90 neutral trials. Perturbed false belief N=757. LLaMA2 could not tell neutral from knowledge-implied (P=0.180, BF10=0.56).
quote: to ensure that models did not merely replicate training set data
limits: Never mentions Morgan's canon. Perturbation results flagged as possibly lower-level than belief tracking. Read to character 100k of 113k.
agent_relevance: A control that separates two causes of the same failure (cannot infer vs will not commit) with a matched manipulation. Copy that design.

source: Strachan et al. (2024), novel items and Clever Hans
finding: They wrote novel items against training-set familiarity and warn that regular structure of false-belief and faux pas items makes Clever Hans solutions possible.
numbers: Faux pas recognition: all LLMs flagged an offensive remark 100% versus 83.61% humans.
limits: Quote fragment only.
agent_relevance: Contamination control needs both new items and cue-removed items.

source: Niven and Kao (2019) Probing neural network comprehension of natural language arguments
finding: BERT's near-human score on the Argument Reasoning Comprehension Task came from spurious statistical cues. On an adversarial set all models fall to chance.
numbers: BERT 77%, 3 points under the average untrained human.
limits: Abstract page only; adversarial exact numbers not read.
agent_relevance: Early LLM Clever Hans case: a lower-level cue account fully explained the pass.

source: McCoy et al. (2023) Embers of autoregression
finding: Accuracy tracks the probability of the task, input and output even in deterministic tasks, a surface-statistics explanation.
numbers: GPT-4 on a cipher: 51% when output is a high-probability word sequence, 13% when low. 11 tasks, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
limits: Abstract page only.
agent_relevance: A specific lower-level account that predicts differences by output probability; test it by swapping answers to rare ones.

source: Ma, Sansom, Peng and Chai (2023) Towards a holistic landscape of situated theory of mind in LLMs
finding: Position paper: current ToM benchmarks cover parts of ToM and are prone to shortcuts and data leakage. They propose 7 mental-state categories and situated evaluation.
numbers: 7 categories; grid-world pilot without numbers on page.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Support for splitting a claimed ability into parts and testing each.

source: Hu, Sosa and Ullman (2025) Re-evaluating Theory of Mind evaluation in large language models
finding: Argues disagreement comes from unclear expectation of whether models should match human behaviour, and from evaluations drifting from pure ToM.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Decide in advance what a pass must mean, before looking at results.

source: Hagendorff et al. (2023) Machine psychology
finding: Proposes using behavioural experiments from psychology to study LLMs; warns that human-designed methods may not transfer.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: The methodological bridge to comparative cognition; borrow designs but not conclusions.
